newsitem.title: UK: UK Conservative quits for Referendum Party.
newsitem.headline: UK Conservative quits for Referendum Party.

text.p: Britain's small but vociferous Referendum Party gained its first member of parliament on Saturday when a member of the ruling Conservatives defected to join the new anti-European political grouping.

The Referendum Party, which wants to secure a plebiscite on Britain's future in the European Union (EU), said that Sir George Gardiner had resigned as a Conservative MP and would represent the Referendum Party in parliament until national elections due by May.

Gardiner was the first sitting MP to join the Referendum Party, formed by millionaire businessman Sir James Goldsmith a year ago to give a voice to widespread scepticism in Britain over EU integration.

He was the fourth Conservative MP to change party in the past 18 months and his move put Prime Minister John Major's government in a minority of two. Two previous defectors went to the minority Liberal Democrats and one to Labour.
Goldsmith announced the political coup at a Glasgow news conference saying Gardiner's decision showed that "country must come before party."
Gardiner, regarded as a maverick and one of the so-called Eurosceptic band of MPs, has fallen out with his local Conservative Party association over previous criticism of Major.
Gardiner said on Saturday that he was "sick to death of equivocation over Europe and the single currency."

He accused Major, who supports a "wait and see" policy over whether Britain should join a European single currrency, of an "abdication of national leadership without parallel in the history of Britain over a hundred years."

Major has battled against the Eurosceptics throughout his six year stint as prime minister and Gardiner's defection will only serve to deepen the rift in the Conservative Party, which is already some 20 points behind Labour in opinion polls.
